result.title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction
result.summary: The world encompasses both physical environments and human actors. Predicting its evolution requires understanding both physical laws and how emotions shape human actions. However, existing world model benchmarks primarily assess physical plausibility and perceptual quality, leaving emotion-driven world evolution largely untested.We introduce AffectWorld, a benchmark that evaluates the chain Emotion-Action-World State through three tasks: World-State Consistency, Emotion-Action Consistency, and Causal Consistency. It comprises 1,498 everyday video samples annotated with plausible emotions, action tendencies, and atomic world-state constraints. A counterfactual subset of 233 samples tests whether changing an agent's emotion under fixed scene and event conditions yields corresponding changes in actions and consequences. We define eight metrics across the three tasks and an additional counterfactual metric, combining automatic visual assessment with human-calibrated VLM/LLM judgments. Evaluations of five SoTA world models (e.g., Cosmos3) required world-state change scores of 0.100-0.280 and counterfactual emotion sensitivity scores of 0.027-0.070 on a [0, 1] scale. These results reveal substantial gaps in generating the consequences of emotion-driven actions and adapting future predictions to emotional interventions. AffectWorld provides a testbed for advancing world models that capture how emotions shape future physical and social states.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AffectWorld 基准，用「情绪—动作—世界状态」链条上的三项任务（世界状态一致性、情绪—动作一致性、因果一致性）加一个反事实子集，配合八项指标评测五个 SoTA 世界模型，结果显示其在生成情绪驱动后果和响应情绪干预方面存在明显差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 其反事实干预设计与因果一致性评测思路，可能为检验 latent 内容对答案的因果作用、以及用 VLM/LLM 评判者做自动评估提供可核查线索。
